fields.meta_title: Retargeting Landing Pages for Warm Ad Traffic | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build retargeting landing pages for four warm audiences, with tagged ad links and every lead saved to a database you own. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build Retargeting Landing Pages for Visitors Who Came Close
fields.hero_description: Build retargeting landing pages that fit each ad audience, skip what visitors already read, and save every lead you win back.
fields.features_heading: What Each Retargeting Page Comes With
fields.features_subheading: Each page talks to visitors who already know the offer, then records who came back and which ad brought them.
fields.feature_1:
One page for each ad audience

Name the audience, such as shoppers who left one product in their cart this week, and the offer it needs. Emergent builds a page around that offer and edits it when you prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Ad tags stored with each lead

The page reads utm_campaign and utm_content from the ad link and saves both with every lead in a database you own. The same rows can sync to HubSpot or any CRM with an API.
fields.feature_3:
Copy written for a second visit

Tell Emergent what the visitor read the first time, and the page leads with what they still need, such as the price or the replay. The introduction they already saw stays off.
fields.feature_4:
Big leads routed to one person

Write a rule, such as teams of 25 or more people, and the app sends those leads to a named rep by Slack or email. Other leads get the usual confirmation and land in the same table.
fields.feature_5:
A second version from one prompt

Ask for another headline or offer and Emergent builds the variant next to the first. The app can split visitors between the two pages and count leads for each in a dashboard.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain now, your code later

Publish on your own domain, which is included and uses credits, and start on the free tier. On paid plans, the full code exports to your GitHub repository whenever you want it.

fields.tab_content_1:
The duvet cover they left, one click from checkout

Marrowell Linen runs one ad for shoppers who left its washed linen duvet cover in the cart. The ad opens a page about that cover alone, with the $148 price and free shipping over $120 up top. Each Back to my cart click saves a row tagged duvet-cart. This week 63 shoppers landed, and 22 clicked back to the cart.
fields.tab_content_2:
Twice on pricing, then a 20-minute demo

People who view Quorvane's pricing twice in 14 days without a trial see an ad for this page. Quorvane sells time tracking to agencies. The page explains seat billing, then offers a 20-minute demo. Agencies of 25 or more people go straight to one rep. Ebberly Studio entered 32, and Yselle Vantrell got a Slack message.
fields.tab_content_3:
41 of 87 no-shows pressed play

Brannigar Advisory had 214 sign-ups for its year-end close webinar for restaurant owners, and 87 never joined. An ad sends those 87 to a replay page that asks for an email before the 45-minute recording. The app matches each email to the registrant list. So far 41 of the 87 have played it, and 9 have booked a review call.
fields.tab_content_4:
Nine questions shrink to three for return visits

Halvercrest Roofing's full quote form asks nine questions. Visitors who opened it in the last 30 days without sending it get an ad for a page with three fields: ZIP code, roof type, and a roof photo. Teodora Quill sent hers from 6 miles away. Requests within 15 miles of the shop go to crew lead Corwin Dellacourt by email.

fields.howto_title: How to Create Retargeting Landing Pages
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to retargeting landing pages that start where each ad audience left off, then build them with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write down who the ad will reach
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Cut what the visitor already read
fields.howto_step_1_des: Name the audience in the ad platform's own terms, such as people who added to cart in the last 7 days without buying. One audience gets one page. When two audiences need different offers, build two pages instead of one that tries to serve both.
fields.howto_step_2_des: A Google Display Network segment must have at least 100 active visitors or users within the last 30 days. Check the count before you write anything. If the list is short, widen the window or pick a broader action, such as any product view.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Drop the company introduction and the feature tour from the first page. Lead with the item or replay the visitor came back for, and keep one button. Write for someone who has seen the offer once and left.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Put the objection you think stopped them in a heading, such as shipping cost or seat pricing, and answer it in two sentences. If you are unsure of the reason, ask five customers who bought on a later visit what made them wait.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Add utm_campaign and utm_content to each ad's destination URL, which lets analytics show the campaigns that bring traffic back. Use one value per audience, such as duvet-cart, and keep it with every lead so the database matches the ad report.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Build the page from one prompt
fields.howto_step_6_des: Describe the audience and its offer, then say where leads should go. Emergent builds the page and the table behind it. Open it on a phone, check the offer sits above the fold, and prompt for changes until it does.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Read results by audience each week
fields.howto_step_7_des: Compare button clicks and leads for each audience tag once a week. If a page draws visits but few clicks, change one thing, such as the headline or the offer, and leave the rest alone for another week.

faq_plan.a: Retargeting landing pages are pages built for people who left your site and came back by clicking a retargeting ad. Each one is written for a single audience, such as cart abandoners. It skips the introduction and opens with the offer that visitor already considered.

faq_plan.q: How do I create retargeting landing pages?
faq_plan.a: Pick one audience in your ad platform and note what it saw on the first visit. Then describe the page to Emergent's AI landing page builder: the offer and where leads go. Publish it, tag the ad link, and point that audience's ad at the page.

faq_plan.q: What should retargeting landing pages change from the original page?
faq_plan.a: Change the opening and keep the facts. Cut the introduction a returning visitor already read, but show the product name, price, and photos exactly as the first page and the ad did. When the ad and the page disagree, the visitor stops to check whether it is the same offer.

faq_plan.q: Can retargeting landing pages bring back candidates who left a job application?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A short page with the role and a three-question application can win back people who opened the full form and left. It works much as recruiting landing pages do for first visits. Check the ad rules first: Google's personalized advertising policy says employment ads may not be targeted to audiences based on gender, age, parental status, marital status, or ZIP code.

faq_plan.q: How long should the ad audience window be for retargeting landing pages?
faq_plan.a: Set it to how long your buyers take to decide. A 7-day window fits a cart abandoner, who decides in days. A 14-day window suits a software pricing page, and a 30-day window a roofing quote. Start short and widen the window only when the list is too small to serve.

faq_plan.q: How do I track which ad sent visitors to my retargeting landing pages?
faq_plan.a: Give each ad its own utm_content value. Google Analytics describes utm_content as the parameter used to differentiate creatives. Two ads aimed at the same audience then stay apart in the report. A page Emergent builds can keep that value on each lead's row in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Should a startup run retargeting landing pages before it has much traffic?
faq_plan.a: Not as a first step. Retargeting only reaches people who already visited. A site with little traffic has a small audience to show ads to. Work on the first page until visits grow, and study the best startup landing pages for how they state one offer above the fold.

faq_plan.q: Should retargeting landing pages offer a discount?
faq_plan.a: Only if you can afford to give it to every returning visitor. A discount on the cart page also reaches shoppers who would have paid full price. Try free shipping or a longer return window first. With Emergent, a second version of the page with the discount takes one prompt, and the two can run side by side.

faq_plan.q: How many retargeting landing pages does one campaign need?
faq_plan.a: One for each audience that needs a different offer. A store might run one page for cart abandoners and one for product viewers. Start with the audience closest to buying, since it has the clearest offer. Each new page Emergent builds sends its leads to the same database you own.

faq_plan.q: What changes when retargeting landing pages are for home buyers or renters?
faq_plan.a: The targeting rules change. The same Google policy covers housing ads, and it applies in the U.S. and Canada only. Point the ad at a page for the listing the visitor viewed, built like any real estate landing page, with its photos and a showing request.

plan.angle: The top 10 for retargeting landing pages is vendor blog posts (Instapage, Feathr, Landingi, LanderLab, KlientBoost) that argue why warm traffic deserves its own page, plus a Reddit thread asking how to set one up. None shows the page after the click with its audience, its offer and its numbers. This page shows four pages built for four retargeting audiences (cart abandoners, pricing-page visitors, webinar no-shows, quote-form drop-offs), each with the ad audience it answers, what the page drops from the first visit, and what lands in the database. The FAQ covers the definition, building one, what to change from the first page, audience windows and list sizes, campaign tags, discounts, hiring and housing ad limits. Dynamic and pay per call pages are siblings and stay out of the headings.
